Author: OptionsHarvest
Text: Early assignment on a short call mostly happens the day before an ex-dividend date, not at random. If the dividend is bigger than the time value left in the call, the holder comes out ahead by exercising early to collect it. So a covered call or call spread that's in the money going into the ex-date can be assigned overnight, and on a spread only the short leg goes while the long leg stays open. On dividend payers like $SPY or $AAPL the ex-date is a second date to watch besides expiration.

Text: Apple plans to introduce stronger privacy controls for Mac users as AI agents increasingly require broad access to personal files and applications. The company said developers have been using “Full Disk Access” in ways that could put users at risk, and it will require a more explicit user action before granting applications access to system files, emails, messages and browsing history. Apple said the risks will increase as AI agents become more capable and autonomous, particularly because these tools can act on behalf of users with limited human supervision. The company emphasized that users should clearly understand the privacy implications before granting such permissions. The move comes as AI agents gain adoption across the industry. OpenAI said more than 35 million people now use ChatGPT Work and Codex, up from 10 million in July, while Meta’s Muse recently topped app-download rankings. $AAPL $META $OPEAZZX.P

Author: topstockalerts
Text: Google has raised the price of its seven-month-old Pixel 10a by $100 to $599, citing higher memory costs as a persistent chip shortage continues to pressure the consumer electronics industry. The increase marks another example of rising component costs being passed on to smartphone buyers, even for older, lower-priced models. The Pixel 10a offers limited upgrades over the 2025 Pixel 9a and uses Google’s Tensor G4 processor, which was introduced two years ago. Meanwhile, Samsung has raised prices on most Galaxy S26 models by $100, while Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max also launched above their predecessors’ prices. Google’s newer Pixel 11 lineup started at $899, $100 above the previous generation, with the company adding more storage to entry-level configurations to offset part of the increase. The range reaches $1,899 for the base Pixel 11 Pro Fold, reflecting broader pressure on smartphone pricing from higher memory and component costs. $GOOGL $SSNLF $AAPL

Text: Is the current AI boom repeating the 2000 dot-com bubble again? $SPY $AAPL $TSLA $NVDA $MSFT There are genuine similarities such ad market leadership concentration, speculative enthusiasm. However, the key differences are far more significant. Valuations are nowhere near dot-com extremes, with the Nasdaq-100 trading around 26x forward earnings versus roughly 60x in 2000. More importantly, today's market leaders are extraordinarily profitable, generating tens of billions in cash flow and funding AI investments from their own operations rather than issuing stock to finance growth. Demand for AI infrastructure is also real and immediate, with cloud capacity, advanced chips, and foundry production largely sold out. A Nasdaq-style 78% crash remains a low-probability outcome without a severe economic shock.

Text: $TMUS Thinking Starlink VoIP kills cell carriers is like believing airplanes make subways obsolete. VoIP doesn't bypass physics. Voice packets are just radio waves. Your phone has a tiny 0.2-watt transmitter. Inside an apartment, office, or parking garage, that faint signal must fight through reinforced concrete, steel rebar, and Low-E glass. Over 300 miles to orbit, the signal dies before leaving the ceiling. Satellite direct-to-cell requires an open sky; it physically cannot penetrate multi-story buildings. What about putting a dish on the roof? That’s not a mobile network—that’s just building Wi-Fi. Urban high-rises already run on 10 Gbps ground fiber, and "Wi-Fi calling" still tunnels straight through T-Mobile's core network to connect. Starlink didn't "win" consumer mobile. It built an outdoor backup for national parks and disaster zones. Terrestrial carriers own the 80%+ of daily life lived indoors. Satellites can't touch that moat. $SPY $T $SPCX $AAPL
